# 10-minute panel script (deck: Student_Success_Assistant_10min.pptx, generated by `python -m ssa.cli report`)

1. **Title (0:20)** — what the assistant does for an advisor at week ~15.
2. **The question (0:40)** — who is still enrolled and at risk, why, precedents, what to do, who first. Population numbers.
3. **Architecture (1:00)** — offline build vs one online service; LanceDB vector store; LangGraph agents; Claude by task
   (Haiku parses, Sonnet writes, Opus judges); the LLM narrates only and everything works with it off; feedback loop.
4. **Honest evaluation (0:50)** — the leakage we removed; same model, two populations; temporal protocol.
5. **Withdrawal risk (0:45)** — ROC-AUC with CI vs logistic baseline, calibration, tiers that separate, capacity lift.
6. **How early can we tell? (0:30)** — four checkpoints; fewer students left to help as evidence grows.
7. **Factors and trends (0:30)** — missed work and inactivity dominate; divergence weeks per module.
8. **Retrieval (0:45)** — hybrid channels in a vector database with metadata pre-filtering; precedents that predict real
   outcomes vs random; one document per enrolment; 6 stories in context, outcome mix of 50 (top-K study).
9. **Prioritisation (0:30)** — learned weights vs v4 formula vs random at 10/20 % capacity.
10. **Agents and guardrails (0:50)** — LangGraph graph; evidence IDs, catalogue gating, critic in code with one revision.
11. **Choosing the models (0:50)** — the same tasks on Haiku, Sonnet and Opus (quality, cost per call); five embedding
    models on the same narratives (accuracy, speed, size). The choice follows the measurement.
12. **Evaluating the AI (0:50)** — five layers: code checks, LLM judge with order-swapped A/B, DeepEval, RAGAS
    (hallucination rate), blind human review against the judge.
13. **The console (0:30)** — course clock, AI text labelled, every view as of one point in the course.
14. **Fairness and limits (0:30)** — gaps tested against chance, proxies, the one real gap and why equalising is a policy call.
15. **Closing the loop (0:20)** — approval-gated learning from advisor feedback; everything regenerated from artifacts.

Live demo (3 minutes, inside the slots above or after them): open the console → BBB 2014J at week 15 → This week
(briefing) → click the top student → Draft a support plan (watch the LangGraph steps) → rewrite the message as a text in
French → scroll to similar students and their full-course activity → Case finder: "repeat students who stopped
submitting" → Copilot: "Who should I contact first in FFF 2014J and why?" (tool calls stream in) → Model quality → AI
features and Human review.
